subject: Subscription renewal: term update, burst capacity add-on, and QBR scheduling
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Marsh <olivia@bluewave.ai>, procure@bluewave.ai
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 Jun 2029 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Subscription renewal: term update, burst capacity add-on, and QBR scheduling

Hi Olivia / BlueWave procurement team,

Quick kickoff note as we approach your renewal window. High-level asks: please confirm these items so we can finalize pricing and scheduling by mid-July.

Summary:
- Current term: 12 months, renewal due 2029-08-01. Customer indicated interest in a longer commitment.
- Proposal: 24-month term with a negotiated uplift on seats and a burst capacity add-on (+20% peak capacity, charged as metered overage).
- Goal: finalize commercial terms and sign amendment before your next billing cycle to ensure smooth capacity onboarding.

Requested next steps:
1) Confirm if BlueWave wants to move to 24 months (we've priced both 12- and 24-month options; 24m includes a 10% unit rate reduction).
2) Confirm expected peak window (dates / expected RPS) so Connor can size burst nodes and run a short throughput test.
3) Schedule a 45-minute QBR to review the amendment, deployment timeline, and onboarding plan.

Proposed QBR slots (PDT):
- Tue Jul 9, 11:00–11:45am
- Wed Jul 10, 2:00–2:45pm
- Thu Jul 11, 9:00–9:45am

I've attached a draft amendment (redwood_proposed_amendment_BW-0678.pdf) and a short QBR agenda (QBR_agenda_BW-0678.md) to give context. If procurement prefers a different cadence or needs PO details, loop them in.

Connor (SE) and Neha (CS) are cc'd for capacity sizing and onboarding planning. Stephanie — can you confirm whether we should include a scoped throughput test and estimated cost for engineering support?

Thanks — looking forward to locking dates.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0191

Attachments: redwood_proposed_amendment_BW-0678.pdf (proposal, 2 pages); QBR_agenda_BW-0678.md (draft agenda)
From: Olivia Marsh <olivia@bluewave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cynthia Lee <cynthia@bluewave.ai>, procure@bluewave.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2029 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subscription renewal: term update, burst capacity add-on, and QBR scheduling

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear rundown.

Quick answers:
- BlueWave is inclined to move to a 24-month term, pending final pricing and legal review.
- We do expect a seasonal peak in late November; planning for +20% burst sounds about right but I'll confirm traffic windows with our infra team.
- Cynthia (cc'd) manages contracts — she'll coordinate redlines and PO timing.

QBR: Tue Jul 9 at 11:00am PT works for our side. Please send a calendar invite.

On pricing: can you include a side-by-side comparison (12m vs 24m) that highlights effective per-token/unit pricing and the modeled monthly cost assuming the +20% burst for one month? That will help our finance review.

Also — do you have a short note describing how burst capacity is billed (e.g., flat monthly fee vs metered overage)? We want to present that clearly to procurement.

Thanks,
Olivia
Director of Product | BlueWave AI
olivia@bluewave.ai

Subject: Re: Subscription renewal: term update, burst capacity add-on, and QBR scheduling

Thanks, Olivia — confirmed for Tue Jul 9 at 11:00am PT. Calendar invite sent.

Connor — can you scope a brief throughput test for the QBR? If BlueWave confirms a November peak window we should run a 30-minute simulated load at ~120% of their baseline to validate autoscale and warm-up timings. Please call out any infra prerequisites (SSH keys, test endpoints) in your prep notes.

Neha — we'll want to document a 3-week onboarding checklist: capacity provisioning, KV warm-up, and an initial QA pass with BlueWave. Happy to take point on scheduling.

Attached is a one-page pricing comparison (see redwood_proposed_amendment_BW-0678.pdf, page 2) that shows 12m vs 24m economics and an explanation of burst billing: we bill burst as metered overage at the agreed rate per vGPU-hour; there's a small buffer credit included for the first month to avoid surprises. I'll follow up with a short line-item summary for procurement before the QBR.

Action items before QBR (Jul 9):
- Olivia/Cynthia: confirm procurement timeline and whether they need a PO before counter-signature.
- Connor: list prerequisites and estimated SE time for a throughput test.
- Neha: draft onboarding checklist and estimated schedule if amendment signed by Jul 23.
- Stephanie: confirm whether we need to budget dedicated engineering support for the burst test and estimated cost.

Jordan

Jordan / Olivia — thanks for the thread. Quick procurement note from my side:

- We can proceed with a 24-month amendment but need the following to start internal approvals: final amendment PDF, redlines to our MSA, and an invoice template for the initial payment.
- Our target is to have a PO out by Jul 20 and a signed amendment by Jul 23 to avoid proration issues for August billing.
- Please send the amendment with a short cover letter that lists the new term, committed units, burst overage rate, and billing cadence.

I've attached our standard procurement checklist and a DOCX with required billing fields (procurement_bluewave_checklist.docx). If Redwood can provide the invoice template and a single-page cover letter by EOD Wed Jul 3, I can begin routing approvals.

Thanks,
Cynthia Lee
Senior Procurement Manager | BlueWave AI
cynthia@bluewave.ai
